name: USAGov
body: Language alternates, a sitemap that matches the pages analyzed, alt text on every image, and Core Web Vitals that pass for real visitors. But its Organization JSON-LD has a logo and URL with no name or sameAs.
lesson: Name the organization and list its official profiles in sameAs. AI answers use them to say who runs the site.
summary: www.usa.gov scores 88 out of 100 (B). 0 checks fail now, 15 are at risk, and 22 pass. Fix first: 20 structured data items miss a property Google expects.

fix.title: 20 structured data items miss a property Google expects
fix.evidence: / Organization lacks name, /phone Organization lacks name, /voting-and-elections Organization lacks name and 17 more.
fix.fix: Fill the missing properties so the item qualifies for rich results.

fix.title: No content security policy
fix.evidence: content-security-policy was absent on the start page. Missing on all 20 pages analyzed. Injected scripts are not limited by the browser.
fix.fix: Start with the Report-Only policy in the fix kit, watch the reports for a week, then enforce it.

fix.title: Referrer-Policy is not sent
fix.evidence: Browsers fall back to their default. An explicit policy keeps full URLs from leaking to other sites. Missing on all 20 pages analyzed.

fix.title: Permissions-Policy is not sent
fix.evidence: Embedded content can ask for the camera, microphone, or location. Missing on all 20 pages analyzed.

fix.title: Tracking tags load with no consent tool in the page
fix.evidence: Google Tag Manager appears in the HTML and no consent platform or Google Consent Mode default was found. In the EU, the UK, Brazil, and Colombia this is a legal exposure.
fix.fix: Add a consent platform and set Google Consent Mode v2 defaults to denied before any tag loads.

fix.title: 1 page asks search engines not to index it
fix.fix: Remove noindex from pages that should be found, and keep it only on private or duplicate pages.

AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page
